newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Japanese visit disputed isle in East China Sea.
newsitem.headline: Two Japanese visit disputed isle in East China Sea.

text.p: In a diplomatic embarrassment for Japan's relations with China, two Japanese have visited a disputed island group in the East China Sea, officials revealed on Monday.

The symbolic visit on Sunday was made on the eve of talks in Tokyo between the agriculture ministers of China and Japan to break a deadlock over Japanese plans to declare an exclusive economic zone around the uninhabited islands.
Known as the Diaoyu islands in Chinese and the Senkaku islands in Japanese, the islands are claimed by Japan, China and Taiwan.
The ownership dispute has ignited nationalist protests in all three countries since Japanese rightwingers built a lighthouse and planted flags there last July.
"The Japanese government finds it regrettable that the two men ignored advice and landed on the island," government vice spokesman Teijiro Furukawa told a news conference.

A spokesman for Japan's Maritime Safety Agency (MSA), or coastguard, identified the two Japanese as Hitoshi Nakama, an Ishigaki city assemblyman from southern Okinawa prefecture and a reporter from Tokyo's conservative Sankei Shimbun newspaper.
The two men landed on the group's largest island from a rubber boat and left about an hour later after taking a walk around the island , the spokesman said.
He said the MSA did not know the purpose of Nakama's visit. Nakama was not available for comment.
"We find it inappropriate to comment individually on our daily reporting activities," said Shigeru Tsujimoto from Sankei Shimbun's public relations department.
